content:
tanya: Heads-up — we should add a Grafana panel that highlights "hot streaks" for GPUs (sustained thermal/power above normal) per rack and flags potential KV cache evictions. Current fleet alerts only look at 1m spikes which misses sustained mid-high heat.
alex: +1. We need both an instantaneous metric and a rolling-window derived series. Something like "gpu_temp_celsius" avg over 5m and a count of GPUs > 80C over 30m.
sam: Can you paste a starting PromQL? I can wire it into the dashboard.
tanya: Rough PromQL to detect sustained high temp (5m avg > 78C for 30m):

```promql
avg_over_time(avg by (gpu_id) (rate(gpu_temp_celsius[1m]))[30m:5m]) > 78
```

(This is messy — maybe better to use recording rules for per-gpu 5m_avg then another rule for streaks.)
maria: I would avoid rate() for temperature — it's not a counter. Try:

```promql
avg_over_time(gpu_temp_celsius[5m])
```

Then a query for streaks:

```promql
count_over_time((avg_over_time(gpu_temp_celsius[5m]) > 78)[30m:1m]) >= 25
```

This returns GPUs that were >78C for at least 25 of the last 30 minutes. Use "count_over_time" threshold to tune sensitivity.
alex: For power draw correlation (to avoid false positives) add a second series: high_temp AND high_power. Example in Grafana expression: `high_temp_series and on(gpu_id) (gpu_power_watts > 220)`
sam: For alerts, debounce at 10m and annotate the dashboard when an alert fires. We should also create a derived metric for "hot_streak_seconds" via Prometheus recording rule to avoid heavy on-the-fly queries.
maria: I'll paste a minimal panel JSON fragment you can import into the fleet dashboard (edit ids after import). This uses two queries (temp_streak_count, power_high) and a transformation to show per-rack counts.

```json
{
  "type": "timeseries",
  "title": "GPU Hot Streaks (per rack)",
  "targets": [
    {"expr": "sum by (rack) (count_over_time((avg_over_time(gpu_temp_celsius[5m]) > 78)[30m:1m]))"},
    {"expr": "sum by (rack) (gpu_power_watts > 220)"}
  ],
  "options": {"legend": {"displayMode": "list"}}
}
```

(deploy CI will validate JSON shape)
infra-bot: dashboard-lint: note: panel JSON uses `avg_over_time` with raw metric — consider adding a recording rule `gpu_temp_5m` to reduce query cost. (link: https://ci.internal/reports/1234)
devin: I can take ownership of adding the recording rules + alerting. Plan: add `gpu_temp_5m` and `gpu_hot_streak` recording rules, then add the panel and an alert with 10m for firing and 15m for critical. Will update PR by EOD.
tanya: Thanks — please add SLO note in the panel: "target: <5% of GPUs with hot streaks per cluster per week" and include runbook link. Also add an annotation on the dashboard for rollouts (we saw thermal spikes after the 2026-11 kernel bump). :wave:
alex: FYI I'll add a Grafana variable for region and rack so we can filter. Also propose a separate heatmap panel for per-GPU thermal distribution (bucketed).
devin: ack, will include region var and a heatmap panel. Assigning to myself now. @sam can you review alert thresholds after PR?
sam: Yup, I'll review. If we see too many false positives, increase the duration threshold and require concurrent power draw > threshold.
maria: One more note — if we see sustained high temps without high power, that's often a cooling/airflow problem. Add an annotation to call out HVAC tickets automatically when sustained temp > 85C for > 20min.
tanya: Perfect. Leaving this thread here so it's easy to search later. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
